name: Camera Obscura
blurb: The optical principle the medium is named for — a darkened room or box projecting the world through a small hole. For centuries an artist's drawing aid; the image could be seen but not yet kept.

name: Heliography
blurb: Nicéphore Niépce fixes the first surviving photograph, 'View from the Window at Le Gras', after an exposure of many hours on a pewter plate.

name: The Daguerreotype
blurb: Louis Daguerre's process — a sharp, unique image on silvered copper — is announced in Paris and given to the world. Photography goes public.

name: The Calotype
blurb: William Henry Fox Talbot patents the paper negative, allowing many positive prints from one exposure — the negative-positive principle behind all film.

name: Wet-Plate Collodion
blurb: Sharp, detailed and cheap, but the glass plate had to be coated, exposed and developed within minutes — sending photographers out with portable darkrooms.

name: Gelatin Dry Plate
blurb: Factory-made, storable plates free the photographer from the darkroom tent and, being faster, make the hand-held snapshot possible.

name: Kodak Roll Film
blurb: 'You press the button, we do the rest.' George Eastman's roll-film camera puts photography in everyone's hands and creates the snapshot.

name: Autochrome
blurb: The Lumière brothers release the first practical colour process, a glass plate of dyed potato-starch grains giving soft, pointillist colour.

name: The Leica (35mm)
blurb: A tiny, fast camera using movie film turns photography mobile and candid — the tool that made street photography and photojournalism.

name: Kodachrome
blurb: Modern, fine-grained colour film arrives, eventually defining the look of 20th-century colour photography.

name: Instant & the Modern SLR
blurb: Polaroid delivers a finished print in a minute; the era of the system single-lens reflex (Hasselblad, then Nikon) begins.

name: The First Digital Camera
blurb: Kodak engineer Steven Sasson builds a prototype that records an image to a cassette tape — the seed of the digital revolution.

name: Photoshop
blurb: Adobe Photoshop 1.0 ships, moving the darkroom onto the computer and reopening century-old questions about the manipulated image.

name: The Cameraphone
blurb: The first commercial camera phones appear; within a decade nearly everyone carries a camera and billions of photographs are made daily.

name: Mirrorless & Computational
blurb: Mirrorless cameras and smartphone computational photography — HDR, multi-frame stacking, AI processing — redefine what a 'photograph' even is.
